label: The numbers
title: Seventeen years of filings: the kiosks, the rentals and the debt
lede: Redbox was never a company with its own published accounts for long. The figures come from whoever owned it: Coinstar and Outerwall to 2015, Redbox Entertainment for 2019 to 2021, and Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment after that. Nothing was published for 2016 to 2018, and the charts leave those years blank.

blocks.title: The rise and fall, in kiosks
blocks.subtitle: Kiosks at each year end, and at the shutdown. The gap is the private-equity years, for which no figures were published.

points.title: 2008: Coinstar takes control
points.text: 13,700 DVD kiosks, a count that includes the smaller DVDXpress chain. More than 3,200 are in Walmart stores.[^6]

points.title: 2013: the peak
points.text: About 44,000 kiosks in 36,400 locations. Only 300 were added during the year.[^11]

points.title: 2021: the going-concern warning
points.text: 38,379 kiosks, and revenue down by two thirds in two years.[^17]

points.title: July 2024: switched off
points.text: About 24,000 kiosks were left when the liquidation was ordered.[^26]

blocks.source: Coinstar and Outerwall 10-Ks for 2008–2015[^6][^8][^9][^11][^13]; Redbox Entertainment 10-K for 2019–2021[^17]; Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment 10-Ks for 2022 and 2023, which give approximate counts as of their filing dates[^21][^22]; Variety for July 2024[^26]. The 2014 figure of 42,280 is the U.S. count restated in the FY2015 report; including Canada it was 43,680.[^12][^13]

blocks.title: The kiosk network, in Blockbusters
blocks.equation: 44,000 ÷ 9,094 = 4.8, shown as 5 stores. Kiosks are from Outerwall’s FY2013 10-K[^11]; Blockbuster’s store count is from its FY2005 10-K[^36]. A kiosk held about 500 to 630 discs[^3][^1], far fewer than a video store, so this compares points of sale, not size.
